correctness.rationale: The seven-point blowup classification gives the four complete curve families. I used an alternative signed-pair model: assign E_i to +{i,8}, H−E_i−E_j to −{i,j}, and each Geiser mate the opposite sign on its pair. For signed pairs (s,A),(t,B), checking the Picard pairing gives intersection (1−st(2|A∩B|−1))/2; the remaining two curve families are the Geiser complements. I constructed the 56-vertex graph using this formula and checked it equals the distance-two relation for intersection-zero adjacency. It has 756 edges and degree 27. The exact characteristic polynomial gives eigenvalues 0(1), 24(21), 28(27), 36(7) for the Laplacian, so it is connected and has 2^128·3^35·7^26 spanning trees, confirmed by integer cofactor determinant. Exact integer Smith form yields 1(8), 2(14), 4(7), 28(5), 336(14), 3024, 6048(6), with parenthesized multiplicities. In particular the exponent is 6048. The classification and pairing model apply to every surface in the stated smooth characteristic-zero scope.

evidence: The weighted multigraph has two additional parallel edges for each Geiser pair; its Laplacian is L+2(I−P), for P the involution matrix. Its group has, among others, factors 560 and 1120, whereas the target has 3024 and 6048.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The relation between the two matrices shares the Geiser-invariant rational restriction but is not a row/column equivalence or a Smith-group transfer. In particular the change on the anti-invariant space and the integral lattice at 2 do not recover the claimed group from the weighted cokernel. The geometric adjacency facts determine the matrix, not its integral quotient.

evidence: The one-skeleton of the E7 Gosset polytope 3_{21} encodes intersection zero, not one. The latter is its distance-two graph, on the same vertices and with the same edge count. The rectified 5-cell is 0_{21}, an A4 polytope, not this graph.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The aliases and distance relation identify which Laplacian must be compared. Equal vertex counts and valency of the two relations do not give an isomorphism; their spectra differ.

value.rationale: The intersection-one relation and its integral divisor quotient are canonical for all surfaces in scope. The 2-, 3- and 7-primary multiplicities refine the distance graph's spectrum and tree count and are a concrete comparison invariant for chip-firing on exceptional-curve graphs. This is neither the ordinary Gosset graph nor an arbitrary subset of exceptional curves, and the full Smith group is not supplied by the geometric distance counts.
